An operator trains an LFM2.5-1.2B-Base adapter with target_modules = "preset:lfm2", then runs sloth export --format gguf --quant q4_k_m for an Orin Nano or --format awq for Thor/Spark vLLM, each producing a self-contained model directory plus export.json, with every step honouring --json, --dry-run and error:/hint:

the same adapter directory produced by sloth train is the input to every export format; no format requires retraining

each docs/tested.md row is backed by a command that was actually run on the Spark in that PR's branch, with the artifact loaded once (llama-cli for gguf, vllm for awq, transformers for merged-16bit, vllm --lora-modules for the LFM2.5 adapter); a format whose live run fails ships as 'not tested', not as supported

When the model id contains lfm2 (case-insensitive) and [hyperparameters].target_modules is absent, sloth train emits one emit_diagnostic hint on stderr pointing at target_modules = "preset:lfm2" (dry-run and real runs) and proceeds. Presets are spelled preset:<name> in the same TOML key that also accepts a list of names or a single regex string. Because Unsloth folds a name list into a tag regex that cannot reach LFM2's conv.in_proj/out_proj (measured live: 0 conv modules adapted from an 8-name list), preset:lfm2 resolves to the regex model\.layers\.\d+\.(self_attn\.(q|k|v|out)_proj|conv\.(in|out)_proj|feed_forward\.w[123]) and the resolved value is what lands in the dry-run plan and training_metadata.json

with an LFM2 model id and no target_modules the hint text appears on stderr exactly once and stdout is unchanged (dry-run JSON parses); with preset:lfm2 the plan's hyperparameters.target_modules equals the documented regex and a fake-backend run records that same string in get_peft_model kwargs

sloth export --format nvfp4 (Blackwell: Spark, Thor) reuses the same llm-compressor oneshot path as awq with QuantizationModifier(scheme='NVFP4', targets=['Linear'], ignore=['lm_head']) and the same calibration data, writing a compressed-tensors nvfp4 layout that vLLM loads on Blackwell; --format awq stays for Orin
one real nvfp4 export on the Spark writes quantization_config.format == nvfp4-pack-quantized and vllm/vllm-openai loads it and generates (measured 2026-09-15 with llmcompressor 0.10.0.3, no shim)

Adding target_modules to RunConfig must not change config_hash for existing TOMLs that do not set it: registry.compute_config_hash hashes dataclasses.asdict(config) (registry.py:147-158), so a new None-default field silently changes every stored run's hash and breaks runs/compare matching — omit None-valued optional fields from the hash (or version the hash) and test that a pre-change TOML hashes identically
tests/test_runs_registry.py asserts compute_config_hash of examples/lora-smoke.toml is byte-identical before and after the target_modules field is added

Calibration data for awq/nvfp4 defaults to the run's training dataset rendered exactly as the trainer renders it (chat template or Task/Input/Output text, _trainer.py:228); export emits a stderr diagnostic when fewer than 64 calibration samples are available (the smoke datasets have single digits) and --calib <jsonl> / --calib-samples N override it
a fake-backend test shows the calibration texts passed to oneshot equal the trainer's rendered texts for the same dataset, and a 5-record dataset triggers the <64-samples diagnostic on stderr

Exports are atomic and named as asked: the container writes into <output>.partial and the host renames to <output> only on exit 0, so a killed/OOM run never leaves a half-written model dir; Unsloth's '_gguf' directory suffix and its F16 intermediate GGUF (2x the model size) are normalised away — final files land exactly under --output and intermediates are deleted unless --keep-intermediate

killing the container mid-export (SIGKILL in a test via a fake launcher that exits 137) leaves no <output> dir, only <output>.partial; a successful gguf export leaves exactly the requested quant files under --output and no F16 intermediate

Export --dry-run reports estimated disk need (merged bf16 = 2 bytes/param; gguf adds an F16 intermediate of the same size; awq/nvfp4 ~0.5-0.6 bytes/param) and free space under --output, and the real run fails closed with exit 2 + hint when free space is below the estimate
export --dry-run --json carries estimated_bytes and free_bytes; a test with a fake statvfs below the estimate gets exit 2 + hint without any container launch

The torch.accelerator.get_memory_info shim for compressed-tensors 0.16 is applied only when the API is absent AND compressed_tensors.__version__ == 0.16.0, lives in one function in _exporter.py with a comment naming the NGC image it works around, and a unit test asserts the shim is a no-op when the API exists so it is removed when the image moves to torch>=2.11
the shim function is covered by two tests: applied when the attribute is missing and compressed_tensors is 0.16.0; skipped (torch untouched) when the attribute exists

Container preflight for merge/quantize exports reports host MemAvailable/MemFree and prints a hint when MemFree is below ~4 GB (Unsloth import CUDA-OOMs on the Spark UMA in that state even with expandable_segments; reclaiming page cache fixed it in the probe), instead of letting the run die at import with a CUDA out-of-memory traceback
preflight reads /proc/meminfo on Linux and the low-MemFree hint text appears on stderr in a test with a fake meminfo; it never blocks the run, only warns

sloth export never overwrites a non-empty --output directory; it exits 1 with a hint unless --force is given (a re-export must not silently clobber a model a lobes/Jetson deployment is already reading from)
exporting into a dir that already contains files exits 1 with a hint naming --force; with --force it proceeds; an empty or absent dir needs no flag

sloth eval --model DIR (mutually exclusive with --adapter) runs the task-schema suite against a merged-16bit, awq or nvfp4 directory in-container via transformers + compressed-tensors (gguf is scored via llama.cpp's llama-completion from the mounted cache); the result JSON carries the same fields as adapter eval plus model_dir, quant_method/format from config.json, so summarize/compare can show quantization loss side by side

one Spark run scores the same eval suite on the LFM2.5 merged-16bit, awq and nvfp4 outputs and the three scores appear in docs/tested.md; a fake-backend test covers the --model branch and the --adapter/--model exclusivity error (exit 1 + hint)

risks.text: unsloth / unsloth_zoo / bitsandbytes are installed unpinned (--no-deps) in the container; the live probes ran on 2026.9.4 while docs cite 2026.6.9 — decide whether t8 pins them (recommended: pin to the version validated in t6/t13)
The torch.accelerator.get_memory_info shim exists only because NGC 25.11 ships torch 2.10; when the image moves to torch>=2.11 the shim test (t9) must flip to 'skipped' and the shim be deleted
QLoRA-trained (4-bit) adapters were not merged in the probes; Unsloth's dequantize-then-merge path is unmeasured until t13 runs a qlora example
Qwen3 through awq/nvfp4/gguf is unmeasured (all probes were LFM2.5); llm-compressor default mappings should fit Qwen3 but the GQA v->o pair may need the same skip
Two concurrent gguf exports sharing the mounted llama.cpp cache could race on Unsloth's prebuilt install (no lock); single-operator today

Disk estimate uses a parameter-count heuristic; a wrong count under-estimates and the fail-closed check passes when it should not — t13 compares estimated_bytes to measured sizes and tightens the constants
